Root cause: Hello @M-Bab, Thank you for the report.

Keywords: H7, STM32H7XX, HAL, ADC, bug_report, medium, bug, needs clarification, dma, HAL_DMA_Abort, DMA_SxCR_EN, GCC

Technical details:
### Bug Summary HAL_DMA_Abort may fail on DMA_SxCR_EN at the H7 (at least M4 Core) on certain GCC optimization levels ### Detailed Description Dear ST support, I found an interesting but hard-to-track bug in the HAL_DMA_Abort function which seems to be bus timing related: The function HAL_DMA_Abort fails (in my code) on the check if the DMA is effectively disabled monitoring the DMA_SxCR_EN register. This happens on the DMA2 + M4 core in the H745 dual core but the M7 core might be affected as well. When it fails it returns a HAL_ERROR (ErrorCode = HAL_DMA_ERROR_TIMEOUT, State = HAL_DMA_STATE_ERROR). But this fails only on the following (GCC) optimization levels: - -O2, -O3, -Ofast, -Os, -Oz It does not fail on the following optimization levels: - -O0, -O1, -Og Here is a potential fix: It does never fail if there is a single __NOP(); between [__HAL_DMA_DISABLE(hdma);](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32h7xx-hal-driver/blob/a1996eed9172b59887bafaaa0ea1816ea14d48b5/Src/stm32h7xx_hal_dma.c#L806) and [if(IS_DMA_DMAMUX_ALL_INSTANCE(hdma->Instance) != 0U)](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32h7xx-hal-driver/blob/a1996eed9172b59887bafaaa0ea1816ea14d48b5/Src/stm32h7xx_hal_dma.c#L825). I will not try to dive deeper into this bug. You will be able to diagnose and improve this situation far better at STM. ### Expected Behavior _No response_ ### Actual Behavior _No response_ ### Environment _No response_ ### Severity Normal

issues.issue_title: [Bug]: `HAL_SD_ConfigWideBusOperation` applies UHS clock bypass on 3.3V bus when `USE_SD_TRANSCEIVER == 0`
issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: [Bug]: `HAL_SD_ConfigWideBusOperation` applies UHS clock bypass on 3.3V bus when `USE_SD_TRANSCEIVER == 0`
Context: repo=stm32h7xx-hal-driver, mcu_series=H7, board=STM32H7XX, component=None, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=high, state=open, issue_number=109
Root cause: Hello @424778940z, Thank you for your report.
Fix: ### Bug Summary When USE_SD_TRANSCEIVER is **not set** (no 1.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, STM32H7XX, HAL, bug_report, high, bug, internal bug tracker, sdmmc, sd, USE_SD_TRANSCEIVER, HAL_SD_ConfigWideBusOperation, CARD_ULTRA_HIGH_SPEED

Technical details:
### Bug Summary When USE_SD_TRANSCEIVER is **not set** (no 1.8V voltage transceiver), HAL_SD_ConfigWideBusOperation() can still apply ClockDiv = 0 (clock bypass) for cards that report CARD_ULTRA_HIGH_SPEED capability. This results in the SDMMC peripheral running at full kernel clock speed (e.g., 100 MHz) on a **3.3V bus**, far exceeding the SD specification limit of 50 MHz for High Speed mode at 3.3V. ### Detailed Description ## Affected Function [HAL_SD_ConfigWideBusOperation() in Src/stm32h7xx_hal_sd.c](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32h7xx-hal-driver/blob/a1996eed9172b59887bafaaa0ea1816ea14d48b5/Src/stm32h7xx_hal_sd.c#L1723) ## Root Cause There is an inconsistency between HAL_SD_ConfigSpeedBusOperation() and HAL_SD_ConfigWideBusOperation(): ### ConfigSpeedBusOperation — correctly guarded [HAL_SD_ConfigSpeedBusOperation()](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32h7xx-hal-driver/blob/a1996eed9172b59887bafaaa0ea1816ea14d48b5/Src/stm32h7xx_hal_sd.c#L1866) uses [#if (USE_SD_TRANSCEIVER != 0U)](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32h7xx-hal-driver/blob/a1996eed9172b59887bafaaa0ea1816ea14d48b5/Src/stm32h7xx_hal_sd.c#L1878) to separate UHS and non-UHS code paths. When there is **no transceiver**, the [SDMMC_SPEED_MODE_AUTO case](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32h7xx-hal-driver/blob/a1996eed9172b59887bafaaa0ea1816ea14d48b5/Src/stm32h7xx_hal_sd.c#L1985) correctly limits the card to **SDR25 (High Speed, 50 MHz)** — it does **not** attempt UHS voltage switching. ### ConfigWideBusOperation — NOT guarded (the bug) [HAL_SD_ConfigWideBusOperation()](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32h7xx-hal-driver/blob/a1996eed9172b59887bafaaa0ea1816ea14d48b5/Src/stm32h7xx_hal_sd.c#L1723) has **no** USE_SD_TRANSCEIVER check. It decides the clock divider based solely on hsd->SdCard.CardSpeed: c // Line 1793-1794 — no USE_SD_TRANSCEIVER guard else if (hsd->SdCard.CardSpeed == CARD_ULTRA_HIGH_SPEED) { /* UltraHigh speed SD card,user Clock div */ Init.ClockDiv = hsd->Init.ClockDiv; // user value (typically 0) → bypass! } [Source: stm32h7xx_hal_sd.c L1793–L1794](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32h7xx-hal-driver/blob/a1996eed9172b59887bafaaa0ea1816ea14d48b5/Src/stm32h7xx_hal_sd.c#L1793-L1794) When hsd->Init.ClockDiv == 0 (which means "auto-decide"), this blindly passes 0 to the CLKCR register, setting **CLKDIV = 0 (bypass mode)** — the SDMMC clock runs at full kernel clock frequency (e.g., 100 MHz) with no division. ## Bug Sequence 1. **HAL_SD_Init()** identifies the card and sets hsd->SdCard.CardSpeed = CARD_ULTRA_HIGH_SPEED based on the card's SCR register / CMD6 switch response. 2. **HAL_SD_ConfigSpeedBusOperation(SDMMC_SPEED_MODE_AUTO)** correctly detects no transceiver is present and only negotiates **SDR25 (High Speed)**. However, it does **not** update hsd->SdCard.CardSpeed — it remains CARD_ULTRA_HIGH_SPEED. 3. **HAL_SD_ConfigWideBusOperation()** reads hsd->SdCard.CardSpeed == CARD_ULTRA_HIGH_SPEED and applies Init.ClockDiv = hsd->Init.ClockDiv = 0 → **bypass mode (100 MHz on 3.3V bus)**. ## Impact - The SDMMC bus runs at **100 MHz on 3.3V signaling**, exceeding the SD specification maximum of **50 MHz for High Speed** and **25 MHz for Default Speed** at 3.3V. - This violates the SD Physical Layer Specification and may cause **data corruption**, **CRC errors**, or **card damage** on some cards. - It happens to work on some embedded SD NAND chips (e.g., ZBIT, MKFD) that tolerate overclocking on short BGA traces, masking the bug. - The issue is particularly insidious because the speed negotiation in ConfigSpeedBusOperation is correct — only the clock divider in ConfigWideBusOperation is wrong. ## Reproduction 1. Use any STM32H7 board **without** a 1.8V voltage transceiver (USE_SD_TRANSCEIVER == 0). 2. Insert an SD card that reports UHS-I capability (common in SDHC/SDXC cards and embedded SD NAND). 3. Initialize with hsd->Init.ClockDiv = 0 (auto-decide). 4. Call HAL_SD_Init(), then HAL_SD_ConfigSpeedBusOperation(SDMMC_SPEED_MODE_AUTO), then HAL_SD_ConfigWideBusOperation(). 5. Read SDMMC_CLKCR register → CLKDIV = 0 (bypass), confirmed by oscilloscope showing 100 MHz on CLK line. ### Register dump confirming the issue SDMMC1_CLKCR: 0x00025000 CLKDIV: 0 ← bypass, no division WIDBUS: 01 (4-bit) BUSSPEED: 0 (DS/HS) RCC D1CCIPR SDMMCSEL: PLL2_R = 100 MHz → SDMMC_CK = 100 MHz (should be 50 MHz max for HS at 3.3V) ## Suggested Fix **Option A** — Guard ConfigWideBusOperation with USE_SD_TRANSCEIVER: c else if (hsd->SdCard.CardSpeed == CARD_ULTRA_HIGH_SPEED) { #if (USE_SD_TRANSCEIVER != 0U) /* UltraHigh speed SD card, user Clock div */ Init.ClockDiv = hsd->Init.ClockDiv; #else /* No transceiver: UHS not possible, fall back to High Speed clock */ if (hsd->Init.ClockDiv == 0U) { Init.ClockDiv = sdmmc_clk / (2U * SD_HIGH_SPEED_FREQ); } else { Init.ClockDiv = hsd->Init.ClockDiv; } #endif } **Option B** — Update CardSpeed in ConfigSpeedBusOperation when downgrading: In the no-transceiver path of ConfigSpeedBusOperation, after successfully switching to SDR25: c if (SD_SwitchSpeed(hsd, SDMMC_SDR25_SWITCH_PATTERN) != HAL_SD_ERROR_NONE) { hsd->ErrorCode |= HAL_SD_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE; status = HAL_ERROR; } else { hsd->SdCard.CardSpeed = CARD_HIGH_SPEED; // reflect actual negotiated speed } ## Environment - **MCU**: STM32H747 - **HAL version**: v1.13.0 - **Transceiver**: None (USE_SD_TRANSCEIVER == 0) - **SD cards tested**: ZBIT SDNAND (ZBSD), MKFD SDNAND (MK) — both report CARD_ULTRA_HIGH_SPEED - **SDMMC kernel clock**: PLL2_R = 100 MHz ### Expected Behavior when USE_SD_TRANSCEIVER=0 , cap the speed to 50Mhz ### Actual Behavior when USE_SD_TRANSCEIVER=0 , blindly apply 100M bypass from sdmmc_kernel clk ### Environment _No response_ ### Severity Major

Key comments:
Hello @424778940z, Thank you for your report. I will share this issue with our team and work on verifying it. I will keep you updated with any progress. ST Internal Reference: CDM0061340

Problem: [Bug]: DMA DBM: transfer-complete callback dispatch appears inconsistent with callback naming, despite release note claiming a fix
Context: repo=stm32h7xx-hal-driver, mcu_series=H7, board=STM32H747BI, component=DMA, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=low, state=open, issue_number=108
Root cause: Hello @L-proger, Thank you for your report, I believe that current behavior is correct and the documentation ([Link](https://github.
Fix: ### Bug Summary DMA double-buffer mode: transfer-complete callback dispatch appears inconsistent with callback naming ### Detailed Description In STM32H7 HAL DMA double-buffer mode (DBM), the transfer-complete callback dispatch in HAL_DMA_IRQHandler() appears inconsistent with the callback naming.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, STM32H747BI, HAL, DMA, bug_report, low, bug, internal bug tracker, STM32H7, DBM, HAL_DMA_IRQHandler, DMA_Stream_TypeDef

Technical details:
### Bug Summary DMA double-buffer mode: transfer-complete callback dispatch appears inconsistent with callback naming ### Detailed Description In STM32H7 HAL DMA double-buffer mode (DBM), the transfer-complete callback dispatch in HAL_DMA_IRQHandler() appears inconsistent with the callback naming. From a user's point of view, the expected meaning is straightforward: - XferCpltCallback -> Memory0 transfer complete - XferM1CpltCallback -> Memory1 transfer complete This is also the natural extension of single-buffer mode, where XferCpltCallback simply means that the buffer transfer has completed. However, the current DBM code selects the callback based on the current value of the CT bit: if(((((DMA_Stream_TypeDef *)hdma->Instance)->CR) & (uint32_t)(DMA_SxCR_DBM)) != 0U) { if((((DMA_Stream_TypeDef *)hdma->Instance)->CR & DMA_SxCR_CT) != 0U) { if(hdma->XferM1CpltCallback != NULL) { hdma->XferM1CpltCallback(hdma); } } else { if(hdma->XferCpltCallback != NULL) { hdma->XferCpltCallback(hdma); } } } f CT = 1, DMA is currently targeting Memory1, which means Memory0 has just completed and is now inactive. In that situation, a user would expect XferCpltCallback, but HAL calls XferM1CpltCallback. Similarly, if CT = 0, DMA is currently targeting Memory0, which means Memory1 has just completed, but HAL calls XferCpltCallback. This makes the callback dispatch appear inverted relative to the completed buffer, which is confusing in practical DBM use cases such as refilling TX buffers on the fly. What makes this even more confusing is that the STM32H7 HAL release notes explicitly mention this as a fix: > Fix incorrect callback execution due to inverted CT bit check condition in HAL_DMA_IRQHandler() API. So this looks intentional, not accidental. Please clarify the intended DBM semantics of: - XferCpltCallback - XferM1CpltCallback If the current implementation is correct, then the documentation/comments should explicitly explain the callback meaning relative to CT and buffer switching, because the current behavior is not clear from the callback names. I observed this behavior change after updating from STM32CubeH7 v1.12.1 to v1.13.0. ### Expected Behavior In DMA double-buffer mode, the transfer-complete callbacks should match the buffer that has just completed: - XferCpltCallback should be called when Memory0 transfer is complete - XferM1CpltCallback should be called when Memory1 transfer is complete This would match the callback naming and the natural expectation from single-buffer mode. ### Actual Behavior In DMA double-buffer mode, the transfer-complete callback dispatch appears to depend on the current CT bit value after buffer switching: - when CT = 1 (DMA currently targets Memory1, so Memory0 has just completed), HAL calls XferM1CpltCallback - when CT = 0 (DMA currently targets Memory0, so Memory1 has just completed), HAL calls XferCpltCallback As a result, the callback dispatch appears inverted relative to the buffer that has actually just completed. ### Environment - MCU: STM32H747BI - Package: STM32CubeH7 - Previous version: v1.12.1 - Updated version: v1.13.0 - Affected component: HAL DMA - Feature: DMA double-buffer mode (DBM) ### Severity None

Technical details:
### Bug Summary The result of this function is not correct anymore. The result is much higher than the expected one ### Detailed Description /** * @brief Helper macro to calculate analog reference voltage (Vref+) * (unit: mVolt) from ADC conversion data of internal voltage * reference VrefInt. * @note Computation is using VrefInt calibration value * stored in system memory for each device during production. * @note This voltage depends on user board environment: voltage level * connected to pin Vref+. * On devices with small package, the pin Vref+ is not present * and internally bonded to pin Vdda. * @note On this STM32 series, calibration data of internal voltage reference * VrefInt corresponds to a resolution of 16 bits, * this is the recommended ADC resolution to convert voltage of * internal voltage reference VrefInt. * Otherwise, this macro performs the processing to scale * ADC conversion data to 16 bits. * @param __VREFINT_ADC_DATA__ ADC conversion data (resolution 16 bits) * of internal voltage reference VrefInt (unit: digital value). * @param __ADC_RESOLUTION__ This parameter can be one of the following values: * @arg @ref LL_ADC_RESOLUTION_16B * @arg @ref LL_ADC_RESOLUTION_14B * @arg @ref LL_ADC_RESOLUTION_12B * @arg @ref LL_ADC_RESOLUTION_10B * @arg @ref LL_ADC_RESOLUTION_8B * @retval Analog reference voltage (unit: mV) */ #define __LL_ADC_CALC_VREFANALOG_VOLTAGE(__VREFINT_ADC_DATA__,\ __ADC_RESOLUTION__) \ (((uint32_t)(*VREFINT_CAL_ADDR) * VREFINT_CAL_VREF) \ / __LL_ADC_CONVERT_DATA_RESOLUTION((__VREFINT_ADC_DATA__), \ (__ADC_RESOLUTION__), \ LL_ADC_RESOLUTION_12B) \ ) This function does not work anymore since the last update. The returned value is much to high. What i have seen between the last version is that LL_ADC_RESOLUTION_16B was replaced by LL_ADC_RESOLUTION_12B. I think this is the error. After i changed this line back to the old value it works again. ### Expected Behavior When i call the __LL_ADC_CALC_VREFANALOG_VOLTAGE i should get a value from about 3000 ### Actual Behavior When i call the __LL_ADC_CALC_VREFANALOG_VOLTAGE i get a value from about 47000 ### Environment _No response_ ### Severity None

Keywords: H7, STM32H730XX, bug_report, medium, bug, internal bug tracker, hal, cryp, AES, CCM, CRYP_DATATYPE_8B, CRYP_DATAWIDTHUNIT_BYTE

Technical details:
**Describe the set-up** Custom board with STM32H730XX. AES CCM encryption and decryption are performed with settings: DataType = CRYP_DATATYPE_8B DataWidthUnit = CRYP_DATAWIDTHUNIT_BYTE KeySize = CRYP_KEYSIZE_128B HeaderWidthUnit = CRYP_HEADERWIDTHUNIT_BYTE **Describe the bug** There is an overflow in the HAL’s CRYP_AESCCM_Process when the payload length is not a multiple of 4 bytes. No masking is applied when the output block is read from the HW output FIFO, that leads to data being written beyond the output buffer. Depending on where the buffer is and if it accounts for required alignment the overflow might lead to different consequences. An encryption overflow example below uses the following key, nonce, ad (_they don't matter much for the issue_): key[] = { 0xf5, 0x95, 0x5f, 0xe1, 0xdd, 0x84, 0x74, 0xfd, 0x85, 0xe5, 0xfc, 0xf8, 0x20, 0x33, 0x70, 0x01 } nonce[] = { 0x26, 0xd4, 0xf1, 0xfc, 0x00, 0x01, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00 ,0x00 ,0x02 } ad[]= { 0x00, 0x01, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00 ,0x00 ,0x02, 0x15, 0xfe, 0xfd, 0x00, 0x02 } Given 15 bytes payload: plaintext[] = { 0x01, 0x02, 0x03, 0x04, 0x05, 0x06, 0x07, 0x08, 0x09, 0x0A, 0x0B, 0x0C, 0x0D, 0x0E, 0x0F } it is expected to produce 15 bytes ciphertext: expected_output[15] = { 0xf8, 0x75, 0xe9, 0x1c, 0xe7, 0xb5, 0xf2, 0x7c, 0x1c, 0x54, 0x6a, 0xd9, 0x87, 0x92, 0xca } in reality it produces 16 bytes where the first 15 bytes are correct (_as expected_), but an extra 16th byte - 0x3e is written: 0x24029898 xf8 0x75 0xe9 0x1c 0xe7 0xb5 0xf2 0x7c 0x240298a0 x1c 0x54 0x6a 0xd9 0x87 0x92 0xca 0x3e 0x240298a8 x00 0x00 0x00 0x00 If we reduce the plaintext to 13 bytes, then we will get 3 extra bytes. Some libraries (_e.g. MbedTLS_) use a single shared buffer that contains both the plaintext/ciphertext and the authentication tag. Because of the overflow, the trailing bytes overwrite the tag section, resulting in tag corruption during decryption. **How To Reproduce** Perform AES‑CCM encryption and/or decryption with the HAL where the payload length is not a multiple of 4, and direct the result into a larger empty buffer than the payload. The output will overflow the expected payload area and corrupt subsequent bytes. **Additional context** A similar approach to https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32h7xx-hal-driver/commit/863ab1fdaa904c8f6630c91acdb455cf99e37473 is required for the CCM parts upon reading data out to avoid an overflow. The CRYP_AESCCM_Process should account for CRYP_DATATYPE_8B and avoid filling the output buffer as *(uint32_t *)(hcryp->pCrypOutBuffPtr + hcryp->CrypOutCount) = temp[index];.

Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, STM32H753, HAL, DMA, bug_report, high, bug, i2c, CR1, IRQ, NACK, ERR

Technical details:
**Describe the set-up** STM32H753 in custom product, compiled with arm-none-eabi-gcc 14.3 rel1 **Describe the bug** https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32h7xx-hal-driver/blob/d649ed2c7784bfbef4be144e7bfd8dbb41dce5c3/Src/stm32h7xx_hal_i2c.c#L2055-L2076 The modification to CR1 on line 2075 races with the IRQ that is enabled on 2072. Even though the TX DMA has not been set up, the transfer *has*. That means that the peripheral will begin the addressing phase, which may lead to a NACK interrupt. If that NACK interrupt occurs between the read and write of the |= operation on 2075, then line 2075 ends up reverting the interrupt enable bits configured by the IRQ handler. In practice, this means that the NACK and ERR interrupts are reenabled, and the STOP interrupt is cleared. This is then a critical failure because a NACK has already occurred, and the HAL needs to see a STOP in order to call the Tx complete callback. In the end, this leads to a situation where the Tx complete callback is never called and you have to abort the HAL to get back to a working state. **How To Reproduce** This is heavily time dependant. This use case is with -Og optimisation, a 210MHz sysclk, and a 52.5MHz APB clock. This issue can be most easily exposed by adding a delay. Change the line: c hi2c->Instance->CR1 |= I2C_CR1_TXDMAEN; To: c uint32_t const stored = hi2c->Instance->CR1; HAL_Delay(10); if (hi2c->Instance->CR1 != stored) { __BKPT(); } hi2c->Instance->CR1 |= I2C_CR1_TXDMAEN; Then perform an I2C transmit to an address that is not present on the bus, and therefore immediately generates a NACK. If the code were race free, the transformation above would never fail. In this case it will fail reliably.

**Describe the bug** An invalid tag is generated for payloads that are not a multiple of 4, as described in [Re: STM32U545 AES GCM Tag mismatch - STMicroelectronics Community](https://community.st.com/t5/stm32-mcus-security/stm32h730-aes-gcm-tag-issue/m-p/806718/highlight/true#M8519). ST Internal ticket number: **210917**. **How To Reproduce** An example STM32Cube-IDE project is generated with STM32CubeMX and attached in the mentioned [community thread](https://community.st.com/t5/stm32-mcus-security/stm32h730-aes-gcm-tag-issue/m-p/807226/highlight/true#M8522). **Describe the set-up** Custom board with STM32H730XX. AES GCM encryption and decryption are performed with settings: DataType = CRYP_DATATYPE_8B DataWidthUnit = CRYP_DATAWIDTHUNIT_BYTE KeySize = CRYP_KEYSIZE_128B HeaderWidthUnit = CRYP_HEADERWIDTHUNIT_BYTE **Additional context** Tag is generated correctly when: * When the input array is 16 bytes, but we decode 15 bytes (_as there is only 15 bytes of data_). * When we dynamically allocate an aligned input array of size that is a multiple of _4_, but decode with real size (_i.e, 15_). * When the input array is in the global scope (_regardless of its size_). The tag is generated incorrectly: * When the input array is 15 bytes on the stack. Tried to flush and invalidate the input memory area, as well as to flush ECC (_as buffers are located within SRAM with enabled ECC)_, no difference. After further investigation, the culprit seems to be the padding bytes. During the encryption, the CRYP_CR_NPBLB is used to let HW know which bytes to discard; However, during the decryption process, it is not used/or available. Here is the debug info, which shows that the input with 16 bytes has explicit 00 padding in the last word (0x00a989d1); whereas when the input buffer is 15 bytes, we get 8a instead of 00 in the last word (0x8aa989d1). Working with 16 length: gdb x/15xb hcryp->pCrypInBuffPtr 0x2402a5d8: 0x13 0xb4 0xc7 0x2b 0x38 0x9d 0xc5 0x01 0x2402a5e0: 0x8e 0x72 0xa1 0x71 0xd1 0x89 0xa9 x/4xw hcryp->pCrypInBuffPtr 0x2402a5d8: 0x2bc7b413 0x01c59d38 0x71a1728e 0x00a989d1 When CrypInCount == 3 p/x *(uint32_t *)(hcryp->pCrypInBuffPtr + hcryp->CrypInCount) $2 = 0xa989d1 Not working with 15 length: gdb x/15xb hcryp->pCrypInBuffPtr 0x24021c54: 0x13 0xb4 0xc7 0x2b 0x38 0x9d 0xc5 0x01 0x24021c5c: 0x8e 0x72 0xa1 0x71 0xd1 0x89 0xa9 x/4xw hcryp->pCrypInBuffPtr 0x24021c54: 0x2bc7b413 0x01c59d38 0x71a1728e 0x8aa989d1 After correction of the padding in the last block (_16 bytes_) of the last writable word (_4 bytes_) the tag generation works fine after decryption, required changes are applied to CRYP_AESGCM_Process in stm32h7xx_hal_cryp.c: diff --- a/stm32cube/stm32h7xx/drivers/src/stm32h7xx_hal_cryp.c +++ b/stm32cube/stm32h7xx/drivers/src/stm32h7xx_hal_cryp.c @@ -3085,10 +3085,17 @@ static HAL_StatusTypeDef CRYP_AESGCM_Process(CRYP_HandleTypeDef *hcryp, uint32_t } /* Write the last input block in the IN FIFO */ + unsigned pad_bytes = ((((uint32_t)(hcryp->Size) / 4U) + 1U) * 4U) - (uint32_t)(hcryp->Size); for (index = 0U; index < lastwordsize; index ++) { - hcryp->Instance->DIN = *(uint32_t *)(hcryp->pCrypInBuffPtr + hcryp->CrypInCount); - hcryp->CrypInCount++; + if (((hcryp->Instance->CR & CRYP_CR_ALGODIR) == CRYP_OPERATINGMODE_DECRYPT) && + (((pad_bytes != 0)) && (index + 1 == lastwordsize))) { + // set pad bytes to 0 + hcryp->Instance->DIN = (*(uint32_t *)(hcryp->pCrypInBuffPtr + hcryp->CrypInCount) << (pad_bytes * 8)) >> (pad_bytes * 8); + } else { + hcryp->Instance->DIN = *(uint32_t *)(hcryp->pCrypInBuffPtr + hcryp->CrypInCount); + } + hcryp->CrypInCount++; } PS: Although the fix appears to work (_tested with input data of 15 and 42 bytes, with and without AD of size 13 and 20 bytes_), I'm uncertain if it's entirely correct; therefore, I'm opening this as an issue. I can also submit a PR if needed.

Problem: LL driver routine RCC_GetHCLKClockFreq ignores D1CPRE divider from D1CFGR register
Context: repo=stm32h7xx-hal-driver, mcu_series=H7, board=STM32H743VIT6, component=None, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=medium, state=closed, issue_number=80
Root cause: Hi @Ilia-Ko, Thank you for this detailed report.
Fix: Hello, I'm using the STM32H743VIT6 board and arm-none-eabi-gcc compiler version 14.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, STM32H743VIT6, HAL, bug_report, medium, bug, internal bug tracker, rcc, CMSIS-, LL_RCC_GetSystemClocksFreq, HCLK, PLL1

Technical details:
Hello, I'm using the STM32H743VIT6 board and arm-none-eabi-gcc compiler version 14.2.0 with -O0 option. I'm not using CubeMX setup or bigger HAL driver in this project, only LL routines mixed with some CMSIS-style register access. It seems that LL driver routine LL_RCC_GetSystemClocksFreq() incorrectly determines HCLK frequency when non-unit D1 core prescaler (D1CPRE) is set. The following behavior looks like a potential bug: 1. Setup PLL1 sourced from HSE so that pll1_p_ck = 96 MHz in integer mode (lines 18-44 in my MRE below) 2. Set D1 core prescaler = 2, i.e. D1CPRE = 0b1000 in the D1CFGR register of RCC block (line 47 in MRE) 3. Set dividers for AHB, APB1...APB4 = 1 (lines 48-52 in MRE) 4. Select system clock sys_ck to be sourced from pll1_p_ck, i.e. 96 MHz (line 53 in MRE) 5. Call LL_RCC_GetSystemClocksFreq(&clk) (line 67 in MRE) 6. Now clk.SYSCLK_Frequency = 96 MHz (correct), but clk.HCLK_Frequency = 96 MHz which is incorrect since it should be HCLK = sys_ck / D1CPRE = sys_ck / 2 = 48 MHz. Consequently, all other PCLKx_Frequency are incorrect as well (96 MHz instead of 48 MHz). Also LL_RCC_GetSystemClocksFreq(&clk) does not calculate clk.CPUCLK_Frequency what looks inconsistent too. Some debugging suggests that this routine [Src/stm32h7xx_ll_rcc.c](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32h7xx-hal-driver/blob/57ed86b4c358e2333a71fd895b17f1ccdb68739e/Src/stm32h7xx_ll_rcc.c#L1731) simply ignores D1CPRE as if it were always = 1. It divides SYSCLK by HPRE from D1CFGR register, but does not divide it further by D1CPRE from the same register. The frequencies are set up indeed as expected, since LED on GPIO PA1 with two LL_mDelay(500) intervals blinks 1 time per second when LL_Init1msTick() is fed with 48 MHz value (see lines 80-92 in MRE). The ignored prescaler is framed in red at this screenshot from reference manual (RM0433 Rev 8, page 350). ![Ignored prescaler](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f4165cc0-e965-44e9-b6b6-2502f5cbdf29) Here is my MRE (the only custom source file 'main.c' in project): c #include "stm32h743xx.h" #include "stm32h7xx_ll_rcc.h" #include "stm32h7xx_ll_bus.h" #include "stm32h7xx_ll_gpio.h" #include "stm32h7xx_ll_utils.h" int main(void) { // Increase system voltage scale to the VOS1 PWR->CR3 |= PWR_CR3_LDOEN; // Ensure that LDO voltage regulator is enabled uint32_t d3cr = PWR->D3CR; d3cr &= ~PWR_D3CR_VOS; d3cr |= (3 << PWR_D3CR_VOS_Pos); // Set VOS1 voltage scale PWR->D3CR = d3cr; while (0 == (PWR->D3CR & PWR_D3CR_VOSRDY)); // Start HSE clock LL_RCC_HSE_Enable(); while (!LL_RCC_HSE_IsReady()); // Wait until HSE becomes ready // Configure PLL1 // 0. HSE @ 25 MHz = REF_CK // 1. REF_CK / PLLM = VCO_IN = 1 MHz (thus PLLM = 25) Must be: 1 MHz <= VCO_IN <= 2 MHz // 2. VCO_IN * PLLN = VCO_OUT = 384 MHz (thus PLLN = 384) Must be: 192 MHz <= VCO_OUT <= 836 MHz // 3. VCO_OUT / PLLP = SYS_CK = 96 MHz (thus PLLP = 4) Must be: PLL_OUT <= 180 MHz uint32_t pllM = 25 << RCC_PLLCKSELR_DIVM1_Pos; // This factor is specific for PLL1 uint32_t pllN = (384-1) << RCC_PLL1DIVR_N1_Pos; // Multiplier for VCO uint32_t pllP = (4-1) << RCC_PLL1DIVR_P1_Pos; // Divider for SYS_CK LL_RCC_PLL1_Disable(); while (LL_RCC_PLL1_IsReady()); RCC->PLLCKSELR &= ~RCC_PLLCKSELR_DIVM1_Msk; RCC->PLLCKSELR |= RCC_PLLCKSELR_PLLSRC_HSE | pllM; // Use HSE as input for PLL RCC->PLLCFGR &= ~RCC_PLLCFGR_PLL1RGE; // Select PLL1 input (VCO_IN) between 1 and 2 MHz RCC->PLLCFGR |= RCC_PLLCFGR_PLL1VCOSEL; // Select low-frequency VCO (VCO_IN is 1 to 2 MHz) RCC->PLLCFGR &= ~RCC_PLLCFGR_PLL1FRACEN;// Disable sigma-delta modulator (fractional mode) RCC->PLLCFGR |= RCC_PLLCFGR_DIVP1EN; // Enable P divider RCC->PLLCFGR &= ~RCC_PLLCFGR_DIVQ1EN; // Disable Q divider RCC->PLLCFGR &= ~RCC_PLLCFGR_DIVR1EN; // Disable R divider RCC->PLL1DIVR = pllN | pllP; // Configure PLL dividers and multipliers // Start the PLL1 LL_RCC_PLL1_Enable(); issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: HAL_ETH_ReleaseTxPacket() can present the PTP TX timestamp of a different packet to the application code if preempted
Context: repo=stm32h7xx-hal-driver, mcu_series=H7, board=STM32H7XX, component=None, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=medium, state=closed, issue_number=73
Root cause: Hello @KarstenHohmeier, Thank you for your report.
Fix: I described several locking and concurrency problems of HAL_ETH in issue #72 #71 #70 and #69.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, STM32H7XX, HAL, bug_report, medium, bug, eth, HAL_ETH, HAL_ETH_STATE_BUSY, HAL_ETH_ReleaseTxPacket, PTP, HAL_ETH_TxPtpCallback

Technical details:
I described several locking and concurrency problems of HAL_ETH in issue #72 #71 #70 and #69. This is another one related to the improper or missing locking via gState and HAL_ETH_STATE_BUSY. If HAL_ETH_ReleaseTxPacket() gets preempted and another call to itself in another threads get scheduled (the functions is racing with itself), then the PTP timestamps stored in heth->TxTimestamp may be overwritten with those of another packet before the application callback HAL_ETH_TxPtpCallback() or heth->txPtpCallback() in the original call to HAL_ETH_ReleaseTxPacket() gets executed. https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32h7xx_hal_driver/blob/ceda3ceeca2ee77a76d2de2ee6b560ad87c90a48/Src/stm32h7xx_hal_eth.c#L1437-L1467 This would cause the application code to read the overwritten PTP timestamp and not the timestamp of the packet it actually sent. This problem could be solved by either locking properly and atomically via gState or by not storing the timestamp in heth->TxTimestamp but in a stack variable in HAL_ETH_ReleaseTxPacket() and handing that stack pointer to the application which would be unique per thread.

Hello @KarstenHohmeier, Thank you for your report. The HAL library is often used in contexts where the end user manages the synchronization of calls to HAL functions. If your application operates in a multi-threaded environment, we recommend using external synchronization mechanisms, such as mutexes or semaphores, to protect calls to HAL_ETH_ReleaseTxPacket().

issues.issue_title: HAL_ETH_ReleaseTxPacket() does not test gState and races with itself and TX functions when accessing TX descriptors and counters
issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: HAL_ETH_ReleaseTxPacket() does not test gState and races with itself and TX functions when accessing TX descriptors and counters
Context: repo=stm32h7xx-hal-driver, mcu_series=H7, board=STM32H7XX, component=None, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=medium, state=closed, issue_number=72
Root cause: ST Internal Reference: 191088 Hello, Please allow me to close this issue, as the fix will be considered in the LwIP interface rather than in the HAL driver (see issue #70).
Fix: HAL_ETH_ReleaseTxPacket() does **NOT** check gState before execution **AT ALL**.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, STM32H7XX, HAL, bug_report, medium, bug, internal bug tracker, eth, HAL_ETH_ReleaseTxPacket, NOT, ALL, HAL_ETH_Transmit_IT

Technical details:
HAL_ETH_ReleaseTxPacket() does **NOT** check gState before execution **AT ALL**. https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32h7xx_hal_driver/blob/ceda3ceeca2ee77a76d2de2ee6b560ad87c90a48/Src/stm32h7xx_hal_eth.c#L1400-L1413 It just runs and modifies TX descriptors, decrements buffer counters and reads state from &heth into local variables. This buffered state can become stale/outdated if HAL_ETH_ReleaseTxPacket() gets preempted and other threads issuing calls to HAL_ETH_Transmit_IT() or HAL_ETH_Transmit() get scheduled instead. Among other things HAL_ETH_ReleaseTxPacket() contains the decrement of dmatxdesclist->BuffersInUse. https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32h7xx_hal_driver/blob/ceda3ceeca2ee77a76d2de2ee6b560ad87c90a48/Src/stm32h7xx_hal_eth.c#L1477 for which the increment has been guarded by a critical section https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32h7xx_hal_driver/blob/ceda3ceeca2ee77a76d2de2ee6b560ad87c90a48/Src/stm32h7xx_hal_eth.c#L3333-L3340 So somebody suspected there might be race conditions there but failed to follow through ;) You really, really, really need to lock this properly with atomic Test-and-Set of gState, because even the read-modify-write of TX descriptor OWN bits is potentially racy (see #71 #70 and #69) This is not a theoretical bug! Under high incoming packet load (~8000 packets per second RX) there are frequent preemptions by the input thread which runs with realtime priority (code generated by CubeIDE). ![grafik](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f3a52b25-3eaf-4ad7-90fe-6b3d20e4e569) This causes the TX calls and TX packet releases in other threads to be preempted and scheduled randomly and thrashes the data in &heth to a point where the system would not send TX packets any more. Under low packet load this can still occur and leads to unstable TX operation where systems will stop transmitting data after multiple days when these race conditions randomly occur but with much lower probability.

Technical details:
HAL_ETH uses gState as a "poor man's mutex" to guard it's internal state and associated hardware registers against concurrent access and enforce a specific order of initialization. Context: repo=stm32h7xx-hal-driver, mcu_series=H7, board=STM32H7B3, component=ETH, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=high, state=open, issue_number=41

Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, STM32H7B3, HAL, ETH, bug_report, high, bug, internal bug tracker, usb, MCU, ASIX, AX88772B

Technical details:
**Description of the set-up** * STM32H7B3 MCU, custom board * STM32CubeIDE 1.10.1 * STM32CubeH7 1.10.0 **Description of the bug** We are using a STM32H7B3 controller in combination with a USB Ethernet Adapter based on the ASIX AX88772B chip and have DMA enabled for the USB Host Controller. We were struggling with DTERR (data toggle) errors when receiving packets from the ASIX chip. Using ping packets of varying sizes we could pin down the issue. Here is the code that was causing the problem. stm32h7xx_hal_hcd.c, lines 1250ff: c if (hhcd->Init.dma_enable == 1U) { if ((((hhcd->hc[chnum].xfer_count + hhcd->hc[chnum].max_packet - 1U) / hhcd->hc[chnum].max_packet) & 1U) != 0U) { hhcd->hc[chnum].toggle_in ^= 1U; } } else { hhcd->hc[chnum].toggle_in ^= 1U; } The else-part for disabled DMA works fine, we have no issues when DMA is disabled. In case DMA is enabled the current implementation only looks at whether the number of USB packets in order to receive xfer_count bytes is even or odd. This totally ignores the handling of zero-length packets that the sender sends according to the USB spec. Here are the proposed changes with explanatory comments that have been verified with 3 different USB device types connected to the Host Controller: c if (hhcd->Init.dma_enable == 1U) { if (hhcd->hc[chnum].xfer_len == hhcd->hc[chnum].max_packet) { /* If xfer_len (the total requested data size) is equal to the max packet size of the USB endpoint then XFRC interrupt will be triggered for each incoming USB packet separately, including ZLPs. Thus we need to toggle on each XFRC interrupt. */ hhcd->hc[chnum].toggle_in ^= 1U; } else if (hhcd->hc[chnum].xfer_count % hhcd->hc[chnum].max_packet == 0) { /* Else, if xfer_count (received data size) is a multiple of the max packet size of the USB endpoint we need to account for ZLPs that are sent by the sender and signalise a completed transmission to the host controller. */ if ((((hhcd->hc[chnum].xfer_count / hhcd->hc[chnum].max_packet) & 1U) == 0U) && (hhcd->hc[chnum].xfer_count != hhcd->hc[chnum].xfer_len)) { /* If the received amount of data is an even multiple of the max packet size of the USB endpoint then we generally want to toggle because of the additional ZLP that is sent by the sender and that does not generate a separate XFRC interrupt with DMA enabled. The exception from this case is if we received the exact amount of data that has been requested. Then the XFRC interrupt will be triggered immediately and the following ZLP will be received as a separate transfer, triggering another XFRC interrupt. In this case we trigger only once on the ZLP XFRC interrupt. This branch also includes the ZLP itself (xfer_count = 0). If we get a separate XFRC interrupt for it, then we want to toggle.*/ hhcd->hc[chnum].toggle_in ^= 1U; } } else { if ((((hhcd->hc[chnum].xfer_count + hhcd->hc[chnum].max_packet - 1U) / hhcd->hc[chnum].max_packet) & 1U) != 0U) { /* If xfer_count is not a multiple of max_packet, then we just need to toggle if the number of USB packets required for the received data is odd */ hhcd->hc[chnum].toggle_in ^= 1U; } } } else { /* With DMA disabled the XFRC interrupt is generated for each USB packet separately, thus we need to toggle every time. */ hhcd->hc[chnum].toggle_in ^= 1U; } Could you please confirm if this is a real issue and not a misconfiguration of our part as well as verify the proposed changes? This problem (or at least a very similar one) has already been reported once here #28, but has been discarded since the bug report was in Chinese. Kind regards Ilya

Note that the pointer cast violates the strict aliasing rule and thus invokes Undefind Behavior, but that's not the real problem here. The actual problem is that more data is read then required in case Size is not a multiple of 4. When pInBuffer is at the end of a memory region and not 32-bit aligned, this can cause a BusFault. For example, when the buffer is located at the end of the AXI SRAM on the STM32H753, reading one byte too much will cause the MCU to read from Reserved memory and thus cause a BusFault. The following example code should demonstrate this: c uint8_t pOutBuffer[32]; uint8_t *pInBuffer = (uint8_t *)0x2407FFD1; // 47 bytes before the end of AXI SRAM uint32_t Size = 45; // 45 bytes (so the input buffer is still completely inside AXI SRAM) HASH_Start(&hhash, pInBuffer, Size, pOutBuffer, HAL_MAX_DELAY, HASH_ALGOSELECTION_SHA256); // will crash A solution would be to handle the last 1-3 bytes (in case Size is not a multiple of 4) separately, thereby avoiding reading out-of-bounds. **Screenshots** ![image](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32h7xx_hal_driver/assets/86773465/1852ddf7-7e79-46ed-b210-307861cac13c)

Note that my remark about violating the strict aliasing rule might not have been entirely correct, but the pointer cast can definitely cause unaligned memory access, which could result in a UsageFault for memory regions that do not support unaligned access (such as the SDRAM). Technical details:
The macro IS_ADC_CALFACT is currently defined (see [here](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32h7xx_hal_driver/blob/12ae8efadd6d8904476b5fbd319e1c266afce734/Inc/stm32h7xx_hal_adc_ex.h#L925)) as: c #define IS_ADC_CALFACT(__CALIBRATION_FACTOR__) ((__CALIBRATION_FACTOR__) <= (0x7FU)) This macro is used to check the parameters of HAL_ADCEx_Calibration_SetValue (see [here](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32h7xx_hal_driver/blob/12ae8efadd6d8904476b5fbd319e1c266afce734/Src/stm32h7xx_hal_adc_ex.c#L270)): c assert_param(IS_ADC_CALFACT(CalibrationFactor)); Consequently, when USE_FULL_ASSERT is enabled in the HAL, the assertion is violated when using a calibration factor with a value larger than 127. However, the calibration factor is 11 bits, so I think the check should be <= 0x7FFU. **Patch** The corrected code should be: c /** * @brief Calibration factor size verification (11 bits maximum). * @param __CALIBRATION_FACTOR__ Calibration factor value. * @retval SET (__CALIBRATION_FACTOR__ is within the authorized size) or RESET (__CALIBRATION_FACTOR__ is too large) */ #define IS_ADC_CALFACT(__CALIBRATION_FACTOR__) ((__CALIBRATION_FACTOR__) <= 0x7FFU) Note that the documentation of HAL_ADCEx_Calibration_SetValue also mentions the 7 bits maximum instead of 11 bits maximum: none * @param CalibrationFactor Calibration factor (coded on 7 bits maximum) should be: none * @param CalibrationFactor Calibration factor (coded on 11 bits maximum)

Problem: DMA2D_IRQHandler called with empty ISR register
Context: repo=stm32h7xx-hal-driver, mcu_series=H7, board=STM32H723, component=None, layer=HAL, issue_kind=other, severity=high, state=closed, issue_number=31
Root cause: I am encountering the exact same issue with a STM32H753XL MCU using TouchGFX 4.
Fix: I'm using a custom board with STM32H723 (144pin), 5inch display (LTDC), external SRAM (FMC), external NOR flash (OSPI) with Touchgfx and DMA2D (double buffer strategy).
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, STM32H723, HAL, high, mw, LTDC, SRAM, FMC, NOR, OSPI, DMA2D, ISR

Technical details:
I'm using a custom board with STM32H723 (144pin), 5inch display (LTDC), external SRAM (FMC), external NOR flash (OSPI) with Touchgfx and DMA2D (double buffer strategy). No OS. I experimented **random stucks of the touchgfx** like described in [this](https://community.st.com/s/question/0D53W00000e067WSAQ/ui-stuck-in-takeframebuffersemaphore) thread. After struggling I found out that the problem was caused by **DMA2D_IRQHandler called with empty ISR register**. In fact, the touchgfx was expecting a call to _XferErrorCallback(hdma2d)_ that never happened and so hanged on. For what I've seen when this _empty call_ is triggered the _DMA2D_FLAG_TC_ should be HIGH, but actually this sometimes doesn't happens. I do not know why this happens (silicon bug? touchgfx clean the flag in particular moment?), but for sure the HAL library doesn't manage this case. So to solve my issue I changed in void HAL_DMA2D_IRQHandler(DMA2D_HandleTypeDef *hdma2d){...} of _stm32h7xx_hal_dma2d.c_ the following line: if ((isrflags & DMA2D_FLAG_TC) != 0U) in if ((isrflags & DMA2D_FLAG_TC) != 0U || isrflags == 0U)

Key comments:
I am encountering the exact same issue with a STM32H753XL MCU using TouchGFX 4.20.0. After some investigation, it seems that the DMA2D_FLAG_TC interrupt flag is cleared in STM32DMA::tearDown before the ISR is executed: void tearDown() { /* Wait for DMA2D to finish last run */ while ((READ_REG(DMA2D->CR) & DMA2D_CR_START) != 0U); /* Clear transfer flags */ WRITE_REG(DMA2D->IFCR, DMA2D_FLAG_TC|DMA2D_FLAG_CE|DMA2D_FLAG_TE); } After the while loop is exited, there is no guarantee that the DMA2D ISR is entered before the write to DMA2D_IFCR is performed. I added the following check as a workaround and the issue doesn't seem to happen anymore: void tearDown() { /* Wait for DMA2D to finish last run */ while ((READ_REG(DMA2D->CR) & DMA2D_CR_START) != 0U); if (DMA2D->CR & DMA2D_CR_TCIE) { /* DMA2D interrupt enabled, wait until ISR has been executed, flags are cleared by the ISR */ while ((DMA2D->ISR & DMA2D_CR_TCIE) != 0u); } else { /* DMA2D interrupt disabled, manually clear transfer flags */ WRITE_REG(DMA2D->IFCR, DMA2D_FLAG_TC|DMA2D_FLAG_CE|DMA2D_FLAG_TE); } } Not sure that's the proper way to fix the issue

Therefore, unless a start bit detected, the receiver does not know exactly when it will receive a data. For USART case this can be driven by the CLK synchronization signal. **Describe the set-up** ST STM32H743ZI STM32CubeH7 HAL Driver v1.10.0 STM32CubeMX 6.3.0 IAR EWARM 9.10.2 LwIP 1.4.1 **Describe the bug** Ethernet reception via HAL driver discards packets and lock-ups if Rx buffers' size is less than size of the packets. For example, I set ETH_InitTypeDef::RxBuffLen as 256 and try to receive UDP packets with 512 bytes of payload. I suppose that an issue is in HAL_ETH_IsRxDataAvailable in this block of code, and if I remove it reception works fine: /* Build Descriptors if an incomplete Packet is received */ if(appdesccnt > 0U) { dmarxdesclist->CurRxDesc = descidx; dmarxdesclist->FirstAppDesc = firstappdescidx; descidx = firstappdescidx; dmarxdesc = (ETH_DMADescTypeDef *)dmarxdesclist->RxDesc[descidx]; for(descscancnt = 0; descscancnt < appdesccnt; descscancnt++) { WRITE_REG(dmarxdesc->DESC0, dmarxdesc->BackupAddr0); WRITE_REG(dmarxdesc->DESC3, ETH_DMARXNDESCRF_BUF1V); if (READ_REG(dmarxdesc->BackupAddr1) != ((uint32_t)RESET)) { WRITE_REG(dmarxdesc->DESC2, dmarxdesc->BackupAddr1); SET_BIT(dmarxdesc->DESC3, ETH_DMARXNDESCRF_BUF2V); } SET_BIT(dmarxdesc->DESC3, ETH_DMARXNDESCRF_OWN); if(dmarxdesclist->ItMode != ((uint32_t)RESET)) { SET_BIT(dmarxdesc->DESC3, ETH_DMARXNDESCRF_IOC); } if(descscancnt < (appdesccnt - 1U)) { /* Increment rx descriptor index */ INCR_RX_DESC_INDEX(descidx, 1U); /* Get descriptor address */ dmarxdesc = (ETH_DMADescTypeDef *)dmarxdesclist->RxDesc[descidx]; } } /* Set the Tail pointer address to the last rx descriptor hold by the app */ WRITE_REG(heth->Instance->DMACRDTPR, (uint32_t)dmarxdesc); } I don' t know the point of this code. I make the polling in while(1), so in my opinion in some calls to HAL_ETH_IsRxDataAvailable it is normally to have part of the packet (in one or several buffers) without last part that is not transferred to Rx buffer yet. Maybe I should poll it in another way, but I didn't find any statement forbidding to do it in while(1). So in my situation this code just discards such packets for some reason. Moreover, as I suppose, last part of the packet then arrives to the buffer, but HAL_ETH_IsRxDataAvailable doesn't see FD now, so it doesn't change firstappdescidx from 0 to something and zeroing dmarxdesclist->FirstAppDesc. After finding LD function returns 1, therefore I should call HAL_ETH_BuildRxDescriptors, that iterates beginning from incorrect (zero) position in FirstAppDesc and really handled descriptors are left with OWN bit resetted. When ETH_DMACCARXDR moves to these descriptors, DMA will go to suspend state. Because of absence of LD bit for these descriptors HAL_ETH_IsRxDataAvailable never returns 1 again. Note. Current implementation of eternetif.c by Cube uses zero-copy Rx buffers' pool, so they need to be at MTU size. I replaced this pool with a real copy to lwip pool as I need to have Rx buffers small. With MTU size problematic code never take place. Note 2. If you want to check a correct approach to implementation of HAL_ETH_IsRxDataAvailable, you may look at ETH_CheckFrameReceived in STM32F4x7 Ethernet Driver, that doesn't have presented issue.

Keywords: H7, STM32H7XX, HAL, ETH, high, enhancement, pbuf_free, HAL_ETH_BuildRxDescriptors, API, HAL_ETH_ReleaseOneRxDescriptor, ETH_HandleTypeDef, new_buffer_address

Technical details:
In embedded IP stack usage (e.g. lwip), which is typically implemented as zero-copy, the presently available interfaces for recycling RxDescriptors is problematic. Ideally, when a packet is received and read out of the HAL, the driver code would pass this buffer to the stack, and would only release the descriptor back to the HAL driver when the stack releases this buffer (e.g. through a pbuf_free() call). Between pushing this message into the stack, and the stack _freeing_ this buffer back to the driver (and thus the descriptor to the HAL), it's possible that additional packets are received that go through this same process. Given the scenario above, in a multi-threaded environment, there is no way to guarantee the order the packets are _freed_ is the same order in which they are _received_. The only support approach in the HAL driver is to free all consumed RX descriptors through the HAL_ETH_BuildRxDescriptors() call, but as the freeing may happen in a different order, this approach may cause descriptors to get re-used before the data has been consumed. Ideally, the user would be able to release RX descriptors in any order and as singalled by the stack through pbuf_free() like calls. A few possible ideas for this would be... 1. Simplest API would be to release the last descriptor (single), but with a new buffer address, for example HAL_ETH_ReleaseOneRxDescriptor(ETH_HandleTypeDef *heth, void *new_buffer_address). This could optionally be extended to take an array or even something like an ETH_BufferTypeDef linked list, HAL_ETH_ReleaseRxDescriptors(ETH_HandleTypeDef *heth, ETH_BufferTypeDef *buffers) although implementing this from the user code with multiple calls to ReleaseOne might actually be a little more straightforward than creating the linked list. 1. API such as HAL_ETH_ReleaseRxDescriptor(ETH_HandleTypeDef *heth, uint32_t index). For this API to work, the user would need to be able to also get the descriptor indices associated with the for HAL_ETH_GetRxDataBuffer() possibly it could be embedded in the ETH_BufferTypeDef or through a separate HAL_ETH_GetRxDescriptorInfo() such that it could then be tracked and freed when available.

issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: HAL_FDCAN_GetRxMessage() evaluates GetIndex value for Rx FIFO overwrite scenario.
Context: repo=stm32h7xx-hal-driver, mcu_series=H7, board=STM32H753, component=CAN, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=medium, state=closed, issue_number=3
Root cause: Hi @rxa1031, Thank you for this report.
Fix: Dear HAL Driver developer, STM32H753 Reference Manual informs below: When an Rx FIFO is operated in overwrite mode and an Rx FIFO full condition is signaled, reading of the Rx FIFO elements should start at least at get index + 1.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, STM32H753, HAL, CAN, bug_report, medium, bug, internal bug tracker, spotted before customer, FIFO, RAM, CPU

Technical details:
Dear HAL Driver developer, STM32H753 Reference Manual informs below: When an Rx FIFO is operated in overwrite mode and an Rx FIFO full condition is signaled, reading of the Rx FIFO elements should start at least at get index + 1. The reason for that is that it can happen that a received message is written to the message RAM (put index) while the CPU is reading from the message RAM (get index). In this case inconsistent data may be read from the respective Rx FIFO element. Adding an offset to the get index when reading from the Rx FIFO avoids this problem. However the below code which evaluates the GetIndex and then the Read RxAddress does not seem to test for Overrun condition. As per above information I understand that code need to be modified to first check for overrun condition is needed. Then in case of overrun condition the GetIndex should be incremented by 1 (based on rollover condition) and then used for calculating RxAddress: /* Check that the Rx FIFO 0 is not empty */ if ((hfdcan->Instance->RXF0S & FDCAN_RXF0S_F0FL) == 0U) { /* Update error code */ hfdcan->ErrorCode |= HAL_FDCAN_ERROR_FIFO_EMPTY; return HAL_ERROR; } else { /* Calculate Rx FIFO 0 element address */ GetIndex = ((hfdcan->Instance->RXF0S & FDCAN_RXF0S_F0GI) >> FDCAN_RXF0S_F0GI_Pos); RxAddress = (uint32_t *)(hfdcan->msgRam.RxFIFO0SA + (GetIndex * hfdcan->Init.RxFifo0ElmtSize * 4U)); } Please share your views. Regards, Rajeev
